editorial.description_en: Stone at the edge of a marsh, holding a green cast from what grows on it. Neutral by the corpus convention, for the same bisector reason as mist moss.
editorial.description_ja: 沢のふちの石のような、緑がかった灰色。

provenance.derivation: Editorial construction, not a measurement. Specified in OKLCh as L 0.700, C 0.014, h 152.0° and converted to canonical D65 XYZ by @irodora/color-spaces 0.1.0 (oklchToXyz), rounded to six decimal places. Re-derivable from this sentence alone.
provenance.editorialNotes: Name coined by Irodora: 沢 (sawa, mountain stream or marsh) + 石 (ishi, stone). It is not asserted to be a traditional Japanese colour name, and the hyphenated romaji marks it as a constructed compound (ADR-0065). "Marsh Stone" is an editorial decision about what communicates in English, not a literal translation of 沢石. Relations asserted from measured proximity under the current engine, not from a source: related is the three nearest in CIELAB — shio-iwa at ΔE00 6.7, suzu-gami at ΔE00 6.8, kiri-goke at ΔE00 7.7. complementary is empty because at chroma 0.014 the hue is not a reliable enough statement to oppose. historicalVariants is empty: this entry makes no historical claim to vary from.
